audit.summary: The pointwise-dimension formula for auxiliary d_E violates triangle inequality; the factor2r excludes the zero-module case; the exchange invariant should not constrain replacement copies to the original kernel; two sharpness proof claims need weaker, sufficient inclusion/rank arguments. Core d_EN comparisons, positive finite-dimensional pruning and corrected exchange, sharpness mechanism, and conditional CI reductions were checked with explicit scope limits.

proposition.claim:
The reviewed source is Håvard Bakke Bjerkevik’s publisher version of record. Its DOI is 10.1007/s10208-025-09695-w (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10208-025-09695-w), published online on 27 January 2025 and paginated in Foundations of Computational Mathematics 26 (2026), 939–998. The acquired PDF has 60 pages; PDF page \(p\) is printed page \(938+p\). This is an online-2025 assignment.

The distinction between a subquotient, an erosion neighborhood, and a refinement is essential. With the paper’s shift convention, \[\operatorname{Er}_\varepsilon(M)\cong
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(M(-\varepsilon)\longrightarrow M(\varepsilon)\bigr).\] A representative \(I/K\) belongs to \(\operatorname{EN}_\varepsilon(M)\) when \[\operatorname{im}(M(-\varepsilon)\to M)\subseteq I\subseteq M,
 \qquad K\subseteq I\cap\ker(M\to M(\varepsilon)).\] A refinement imposes this condition on each indecomposable summand separately. Pointwise finite dimension (pfd) permits the decomposition arguments; a finite uniform bound \(r=\operatorname{supdim}M\) is additionally used in the main stability estimate. The report checks these different hypotheses separately.

Printed pointwise-dimension d_E fails triangle inequality.

Withdraw distance designation or supply an appropriate invariant/order with proof.

Require r>=1 or replace r bymax{1,r}; same boundary qualification for related conjectured upper bound.

Allow replacement copies in ambient Nbar, keeping conditions(i)-(iii) and original kernel summands.
